results.title: China-Aligned Hackers Hijack Sogou Input Method DNS Requests to Deploy DarkVigil Backdoor
results.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
results.content:
A China-aligned threat actor known as SlippyNunchucks has been attributed to a Domain Name System (DNS) hijacking operation abusing insecure HTTP communications in Windows versions of Sogou Input Method as part of a surveillance campaign designed to deploy an implant called DarkVigil (aka FDMTP).
The campaign, observed starting July 1, 2026, is assessed to have targeted organizations and Chinese-speaking individuals in Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, and Sri Lanka, according to ESET.
"DarkVigil implants are typically deployed through popular Chinese applications," ESET researcher Anh Ho said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "By abusing these applications, the SlippyNunchucks threat actor has been able to reach Chinese-speaking users across Asia and Europe."
Some of the applications abused by the adversary include Sogou Input Method, QuickFox, QingTalk, MiYunChat, SoftCam, and tawk.to.
Active since at least September 15, 2023, SlippyNunchucks is known for targeting organizations and Chinese-speaking individuals across South and East Asia. These attacks lead to the deployment of a modular .NET framework that includes DarkVigil and a set of over 20 plugins.
Although the use of the backdoor has been previously linked to Mustang Panda, ESET said it found no tactical overlaps between the threat actor and DarkVigil-related activity in its telemetry, prompting it to classify it as a distinct intrusion set.
Earlier this August, Fortinet's FortiGuard Incident Response Team detailed the threat actor's supply chain compromise of the QuickFox VPN and network acceleration tool to deliver DarkVigil.
According to the Slovakian cybersecurity company, the adversary shifted to exploiting Sogou Input Method, a popular Chinese-language input method editor developed by Tencent, as a delivery vector three days after QuickFox released a clean version of its program.
Specifically, the attack involves hijacking the app's branded vocabulary promotion mechanism to serve a malicious configuration, which ultimately paves the way for the deployment of the malware via SGTool.exe, a legitimate Sogou Input Method component that functions as a multi-purpose task dispatcher.
In a clean environment, the executable sends an HTTP request to the "config.pinyin.sogou[.]com/api/brandScd/getBrandScd.php" endpoint to fetch a configuration. But in the attack discovered by ESET, the DNS resolution of the domain is tampered with to resolve it to one of the two staging servers -
- 47.239.250[.]102 (sogou-cdn[.]com)
- 47.237.122[.]175 (dev.soft-png-cdn.com)
The consequence of this DNS hijacking was that HTTP requests to the "getBrandScd.php" endpoint were routed to one of the staging servers, which then responded with a malicious configuration. The configuration, for its part, instructs the binary to download two additional payloads from "sogou-cdn[.]com" and launch the malware via DLL sideloading -
- A legitimate Adobe executable ("biz_helper.exe")
- A rogue DLL ("libcef.dll") containing DarkVigil
DarkVigil is notable for its use of Duplex Message Transport Protocol (DMTP) for command-and-control (C2), allowing the client to execute and orchestrate plugins received from an attacker-controlled server to facilitate persistence or data collection.
Following responsible disclosure, Tencent addressed the vulnerability (CVE-2026-120422) in version 16.10, released on October 29, 2026, by migrating the affected HTTP requests to HTTPS.
SlippyNunchucks is suspected to operate keeping the interests of the Chinese government in mind, with ESET describing it as a nation-state surveillance effort.
"Although SlippyNunchucks targets organizations and individuals across multiple sectors, we discovered significant surveillance activity against an organization operating Chinese-language online betting platforms in Sri Lanka, Hong Kong, and the Philippines," ESET said.
"The targeting of this organization is notable given China's restrictions on gambling, including criminal penalties for operating gambling businesses and organizing Chinese citizens to gamble abroad."
This is not the first time China-nexus threat actors have weaponized the Sogou Input Method as an entry point for malware distribution. In September 2026, Gen Digital said a now-patched vulnerability in the input method editor (CVE-2026-51990) was exploited by UNC3569 to deliver a backdoor dubbed GRAYRABBIT by means of a crafted link.
"The vulnerability chains three separate weaknesses into a single, one-click exploit: unvalidated command-line argument injection in the sgbiz: custom protocol handler, unrestricted URL navigation in a CEF-based WebView, and a severely outdated, unsandboxed Chromium browser engine [susceptible to CVE-2021-38003]," Gen Digital said.
results.summary:
The China-aligned threat actor SlippyNunchucks is exploiting insecure HTTP communications in the Sogou Input Method to deploy the DarkVigil surveillance implant across multiple Asian and European nations.

### Key Points
- SlippyNunchucks has targeted organizations and individuals in Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, and Sri Lanka since July 2026.
- The attack uses DNS hijacking to intercept HTTP requests and deliver malicious configurations via the legitimate Sogou component SGTool.exe.
- DarkVigil is a modular .NET framework that utilizes over 20 plugins and the Duplex Message Transport Protocol for command-and-control operations.
- Other applications compromised by the group include QuickFox, QingTalk, MiYunChat, SoftCam, and tawk.to.
- Tencent patched the underlying vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-120422, in version 16.10 of the Sogou Input Method on October 29, 2026.

### Why it Matters
This campaign highlights the significant risks posed by supply chain compromises that weaponize widely used, trusted software to bypass traditional security perimeters. By forcing a transition from insecure HTTP to encrypted HTTPS, the patch mitigates this specific vector, but the incident underscores the ongoing threat of nation-state actors targeting Chinese-speaking populations globally.

results.title: SanDisk’s Extreme Portable SSD (V3) hits 2,000MB/s as the V3 pair rolls out
results.author: Allie Nguyen
results.content:
SanDisk’s Extreme Portable SSD (V3) reads at up to 2,000MB/s, nearly twice the Extreme it replaces, in a sealed body that weighs 46.9 grams.
Its cheaper sibling, the SanDisk Portable SSD (V3), drops the sealing to stay lighter. Both are already on sale in the US through SanDisk’s store and US retailers.
SanDisk Extreme Portable SSD (V3) 1TB: $239.50 at Amazon
SanDisk Portable SSD (V3) 1TB: $159.99 at Amazon
Will your laptop actually get the Extreme’s top speed?
Only if it has a 20Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 2×2 port. On a slower port, you get a slower drive. Writes run up to 1,700MB/s on the 1TB, 2TB and 4TB models.
The body earns the Extreme name this time. It’s rated IP65 against dust and water, survives drops up to 3 meters, and carries 256-bit AES hardware encryption with password protection.
At 85.09 x 50.8 x 9.91mm it slides into a shirt pocket, and the warranty runs five years.
Can you live without the sealing?
The Portable (V3) tops out at 1,000MB/s on a 10Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 2 connection. SanDisk publishes no write figure for it and says writes run lower, so treat it as a read-first drive. Capacities run 500GB to 2TB.
There’s no IP rating, and drop protection stops at 2 meters. In exchange it weighs 33.2 grams, has a carabiner loop for clipping to a bag, and comes with a three-year warranty.
It’s the drive you toss in a jacket pocket and forget until the day you need it.
Is it time to retire your old SanDisk drive?
If it’s the previous Extreme (SDSSDE61) or the old entry-level Portable SSD, the V3 pair is a clear step up on both lines, and you no longer have to pay for the Extreme PRO to get the faster connection.
Buy the Extreme (V3) if the drive works for a living: big project files, footage off a camera card, a bag that rides in the rain. Buy the Portable (V3) if it lives in a pocket as a backup. The Extreme is the better drive. The Portable is the better spare.
SanDisk Extreme Portable SSD (V3) 1TB: $239.50 at Amazon
SanDisk Portable SSD (V3) 1TB: $159.99 at Amazon
results.summary:
SanDisk has launched its V3 series of portable solid-state drives, featuring the high-performance Extreme model with 2,000MB/s read speeds and a more affordable, lightweight standard Portable version.

### Key Points
- The SanDisk Extreme Portable SSD (V3) offers read speeds up to 2,000MB/s and write speeds up to 1,700MB/s using a USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 connection.
- The Extreme (V3) features an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, 3-meter drop protection, and 256-bit AES hardware encryption.
- The standard SanDisk Portable SSD (V3) reaches read speeds of 1,000MB/s and includes a carabiner loop for portability.
- The Extreme (V3) is available in capacities up to 4TB with a five-year warranty, while the Portable (V3) ranges from 500GB to 2TB with a three-year warranty.
- Both drives are currently available for purchase through major US retailers, with the 1TB Extreme priced at $239.50 and the 1TB Portable at $159.99.

### Why it Matters
These new drives provide significant performance upgrades for users needing faster data transfers for professional media workflows or reliable mobile backups. Choosing between the two models allows consumers to balance the need for rugged, high-speed hardware against the convenience of a lightweight, budget-friendly storage solution.

results.title: The GOP Deserved to Lose — and I Say That as a Former Trump Voter
results.author: Mike Adams
results.content:
The midterm elections are now decided, and the Republican Party was handed a devastating defeat. I've watched this train wreck coming for years, and I'm here to tell you plainly: they deserve every ounce of the shellacking they received. The corporate media will spin the post-election narrative to blame conservative voters for staying home, for being purists, for refusing to hold their noses and pull the lever for the lesser of two evils. But that narrative is a lie. The fault lies with the party itself [1].
I am not neutral, and I won't pretend to be. I voted for Donald Trump twice, and I have watched the Republican Party betray every principle it claimed to stand for. I've also been clear that the Democrats are corrupt -- deeply, institutionally corrupt -- but that does not obligate me to reward Republican betrayal with my vote. This isn't team sports. It's not about red versus blue. It's about putting America first, and the GOP failed that test spectacularly.
We are living through a political moment of profound clarity. The return of Donald Trump to the White House has not been a restoration but a revelation. It has ripped away the final pretenses, exposing the MAGA movement for what it truly is: a cult of obedience, not a coalition of principle [2]. I say that as someone who initially believed in the movement -- not the man, but the principles. In 2016 and 2020, I cast my ballot for peace, clean food, national sovereignty, and a movement that promised to dismantle a corrupt, globalist establishment [3]. What we got instead was something else entirely.
I refuse to vote for "traders" -- politicians who put Israel ahead of the United States. That's the word I use deliberately: traders. They trade American interests for foreign favors. They trade our soldiers' lives for another country's wars. They trade our sovereignty for the approval of a foreign lobby. Governor Greg Abbott, Senator Ted Cruz, and candidates like Mike Rogers embody this sellout mentality. They wave the flag while serving a different master. That's why Rogers and Abbott both lost, and if Cruz had been on the ballot, he would have lost, too.
The Republican Party mocks transgender insanity -- and rightly so -- while letting Texas self-identify as Israel. I will not support that. The GOP likes to talk about borders, but it's remarkably silent about the border between American interests and Israeli interests. The pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC has worked tirelessly to portray an apartheid regime that is committing genocide as a warm and friendly country, and for a long time, US voters didn't question it. Now, finally, US voters have started to wise up [4].
This is not complicated. I believe that America's foreign policy should serve America -- not Benjamin Netanyahu, not AIPAC, not the Greater Israel project. When politicians put a foreign country's interests ahead of our own, they are not conservatives. They are traders. And I will not vote for them.
I voted for Trump twice. I want that on the record. But I am no loyalist and no fanboy -- not to Trump, not to Musk, not to anyone. My support was never about the man; it was about the principles. I believed in peace, in clean food, in national sovereignty, and in taking on a corrupt, globalist establishment. But his administration became something else entirely: a money-grubbing crime cartel. The crypto rug pull, the tariff insider trading, the foreign billions flowing to his family -- these are not the actions of a movement committed to putting America first.
Hunter Biden's Burisma payoffs look small by comparison. I've written before about how the Hunter Biden scandal was suppressed by Big Tech and the corporate media, with Twitter and Facebook blocking access to a New York Post story about his emails [5]. I called it what it was. But the corruption on the Republican side now dwarfs it. I support investigations, prosecutions, and restitution -- not just for Democrats, but for Republicans too. The rule of law should be blind to party affiliation.
Trump has demonstrated an unprecedented lawlessness that exposes the MAGA cult and, impossibly, makes the Biden era look almost stately by comparison [6]. I say that without affection for Biden. I say it as a patriot who is watching his country's institutions being dismantled for personal profit. When I fight for election integrity, I'm not fighting for a man; I'm fighting for the future of every American [7]. That's why I can't look away now.
Trump has ruined the GOP's reputation for a generation, and the party may never recover. I have been warning about this trajectory for years. The only real question is not who wins in 2028 -- it's how long the American empire has left. Trump has sabotaged the military, the currency, trade policy, the rule of law, and public trust. He is a chaos agent for America, and the evidence is everywhere.
I've written about how federal health agencies cannot be reformed from the inside -- not by RFK Jr., not by anyone working within the system [8]. The same logic applies to the GOP. You cannot reform a party that has become a vehicle for one man's ego and profit. The entire Western world is being led off a cliff by individuals who wield power without regard for its consequences. These people have weaponized systems -- including the dollar, SWIFT, and cultural exports -- to further their agenda, and they appear to be beyond accountability [9].
This is not about policy differences. It's about decay. The Republican Party promised fiscal responsibility while racking up a $3.3 trillion debt bill and stalling economic reforms that sparked fears of an imminent crisis [10]. That's not incompetence; it's betrayal. And betrayal has consequences. The party deserved to lose, and it deserved to lose badly [11].
I am skeptical of third-party runs by Tucker Carlson, Joe Kent, or Marjorie Taylor Greene. I admire Tucker for exposing how endless war is an engine of corruption and control [12]. I respect MTG for walking away from a two-party betrayal [13]. But a third party cannot control the agencies, the Congress, or the judiciary. It cannot reform what is fundamentally broken. Running a third-party candidate is like putting a band-aid on a bullet wound.
Unelected bureaucracies like the FDA are unconstitutional and cannot be reformed from the inside. I've argued this repeatedly: the FDA, CDC, and HHS can never be reformed because they are designed to protect corporate profits, not human health [8]. The same is true of the broader administrative state. You cannot vote your way out of a system that was never designed to be accountable to voters. Collapse is the only reform.
Colonel Douglas McGregor is right: financial collapse is coming, worse than 2008 or the dot-com crash. This will be a mercy killing for the empire. I've warned repeatedly that the dollar is on the brink of collapse and that the only honest money is gold and silver [14]. I believe that physical precious metals are the only reliable hedge against the coming devaluation. When the financial reset hits, those holding real assets will survive; those holding digital promises will be wiped out. This collapse will be chaotic and painful, but it will also be a necessary correction.
Trump is an accelerationist of collapse, doing America a twisted favor by speeding the demise of the corrupt empire. From the ashes may come something else entirely -- perhaps a technocracy of AI, automation, surveillance, and internet voting. I do not expect anyone in power to push for a revival of liberty. I expect a transformation, and not necessarily a benign one.
If voting could change anything, they would have outlawed it long ago. Voting is not a pathway to real change; it is a pressure-release valve that keeps the masses docile while the system continues its decay. Prepare for dark, interesting times. The collapse is coming. The only question is what rises from the rubble -- and whether anything worth saving survives.
For those who want to prepare, I recommend studying real history and economics, buying physical gold and silver, and building local resilience. The system will not save you. You have to save yourself.

results.title: N Korea fires multiple missiles, denies US claims on Binance hack
results.author: Al Jazeera Staff
results.content:
North Korea has fired several missiles into the Sea of Japan, according to South Korea’s military, hours after Pyongyang denied allegations that it was behind the theft of more than $6bn in crypto assets from Binance.
South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said on Wednesday that it had detected the launch of several missiles from the Sondok area on North Korea’s eastern coast towards the Sea of Japan.
It said authorities in South Korea and the United States were analysing the details of the launches.
The tests marked Pyongyang’s fourth such weapons launch in a month. They came a day after North Korea denied involvement in the Binance hack, dismissing an FBI announcement that North Korean hackers were responsible as “a trite provocation”.
Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Friday that hackers stole more than $6bn in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record.
The FBI later said North Korean hackers had orchestrated the theft, attributing it to a hacking group known as TraderTraitor, which was also behind a $1.5bn hack of the Bybit exchange last year.
Early on Wednesday, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said Pyongyang viewed the FBI announcement as “an extension of Washington’s invariable hostile policy toward” North Korea.
She ruled out dialogue with Washington until the US abandoned that policy.
“It is our clear stand that we have no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons,” she said. “The choice for peace includes dialogue, of course, but this is not surely equated with national interests for us.”
US President Donald Trump said in August that he plans to meet Kim Jong Un later this year, seeking to revive the bond he claims to have forged with the North Korean leader during his first term.
Trump said it was important to “get along” with Kim, adding that Pyongyang had 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons.
Previous rounds of talks between Kim and Trump in 2019 abruptly ended amid disagreements over Pyongyang’s nuclear programme. In October, the US, South Korea and Japan again reiterated their call for the “complete denuclearisation” of the Korean Peninsula.
The call came as North Korea has accelerated its weapons testing this year, in what analysts say is likely a bid to increase its leverage in any future diplomacy with the US.
Its recent tests have included a submarine-launched ballistic missile, hypersonic missiles, attack drones, and cluster bombs designed to be carried by ballistic missiles.
On Tuesday, Pyongyang said it had tested a new cluster warhead for strategic cruise missiles the previous day, claiming it could destroy an area of 5 to 6 hectares (12 to 15 acres) with “high-density power”.
The latest launches followed a North Korean state media report that Kim had visited a naval shipyard building a destroyer and stressed the importance of a powerful navy.
results.summary:
North Korea launched several missiles into the Sea of Japan on Wednesday, marking the country's fourth weapons test this month amid rising tensions over alleged cryptocurrency theft.

### Key Points
- South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff detected multiple missile launches originating from the Sondok area on North Korea’s eastern coast.
- The FBI recently attributed a record $6 billion cryptocurrency heist from Binance to the North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor.
- Pyongyang officially denied involvement in the Binance hack, labeling the FBI’s findings as a hostile provocation by the United States.
- Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, rejected future dialogue with Washington, citing the current hostile policy toward her nation.
- North Korea has accelerated its weapons testing program this year, recently demonstrating new cluster warheads and naval development projects.

### Why it Matters
These repeated missile tests signal a hardening stance from Pyongyang as it attempts to gain leverage for potential future diplomatic negotiations with the United States. The ongoing conflict over cybercrime allegations further complicates international efforts to denuclearize the Korean Peninsula and stabilize regional security.

results.title: Texas just went blue, and the tech bros are sad
results.author: Ben Shimkus
results.content:
Texas — with its cowboy hats, slow-smoked barbecue, and de-regulatory stance — was supposed to be the California antidote for tech bros fed up with Silicon Valley's Democratic politics.
Well, Texas just got a lot bluer.
On Tuesday, voters handed Democrats control of the House and Senate. In Texas, they selected James Talarico for the Senate and Gina Hinojosa for the governor's mansion, despite massive Republican spending backed by Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
Now, the tech-world frustration is starting to trickle out.
"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," Musk wrote on X.
Jason Calacanis, a tech investor and co-host of the "All-In Podcast," had a similar reaction.
"I never expected Texas to turn blue," he wrote on X. "Ugh, I moved here to get away from the left lunacy!"
Chamath Palihapitiya, another "All-In" co-host, was more dire during a Tuesday-night livestream.
"There's only one thing that sinks the US economy," he said. "That's the AI trade. And the only way to sink the AI trade is to sink the data centers. And the only way to sink the data centers is to sink the power. And all the power that matters right now is in West Texas."
Alex Cohen, the Texas-based CEO and cofounder of AI healthcare company Hello Patient, had a blunter response on X: "RIP AI it was fun while it lasted."
The Lone Star State had not elected a statewide Democratic candidate since Ann Richards won the governor's race in 1990. Talarico is the first Democrat to win a Texas Senate election since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.
Not everyone in tech is angry at the results. LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman, a prominent donor for Democrats, called the midterm elections, including the Texas results, "an overwhelming wave against Trump and his cronies," in a post on X.
As of publication, several outspoken Texas-based tech figures — including David Sacks, Travis Kalanick, and Blockchain co-CEO Lane Kasselman — had not posted about the results.
results.summary:
Texas voters elected Democrats James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa to key state offices, marking a significant political shift that has sparked concern among prominent tech industry leaders.

### Key Points
- Democrats James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa won Senate and gubernatorial races, ending decades of Republican dominance in Texas statewide elections.
- Elon Musk, Jason Calacanis, and other tech figures expressed frustration on X, citing concerns over the state's changing political landscape.
- Chamath Palihapitiya warned that the shift could threaten the AI industry by impacting power infrastructure and data centers located in West Texas.
- LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman praised the election results as a significant political victory against Donald Trump and his allies.
- This election marks the first time a Democrat has won a Texas Senate seat since 1988 and a gubernatorial race since 1990.

### Why it Matters
The political shift in Texas challenges the state's reputation as a deregulated haven for tech companies seeking to escape California's legislative environment. This transition could influence future corporate investment strategies and the stability of critical infrastructure projects, such as AI-focused data centers, within the region.

results.title: The power of sync
results.author: Seth Godin
results.content:
There’s an overlooked power tool right in front of us. Every individual and organization can use it well, but rarely does. I could write a book on this, but here’s the post instead:
Synchronized work happens together, on a shared schedule, in real time.
Asynchronized work (my spellchecker says this isn’t a real word) happens on our schedule.
Phone calls are sync. Texts are async.
Network TV was sync. Youtube and Netflix are async.
Writing a screenplay is async. Making a movie from that screenplay is sync. Going to opening night is sync, watching it two months later online is async.
Writing a book is async. Publishing a book is sync. Reading it is async.
A staff meeting is sync. A memo is async.
Commercial air travel is sync. A private jet is async.
Each offers costs and advantages.
When I go to a live concert, it’s happening. For me, for the audience, for the act. If any of us is having a bad day, it detracts from the experience. But when it’s right and it’s real, magic ensues. It’s largely unrelated from the experience of listening to the same song streamed (async) or on the radio (a blend of the two).
I imagine that your energy levels and mood fluctuate during the day. When working on async projects, the smart path is to match your internal energy with the work to be done. Write blog posts when you’re on a post-swim high, pay bills when all you can manage is clerical work.
Organizations that don’t account for the cost of sync-meetings waste not just billions of dollars but the insight and energy of the people who might be able to contribute if the timing and approach were different.
Sync has three advantages:
- Energy multiplies. When someone is contributing, others seek to catch up. When someone has a good idea, others might work to top it. We have the chance to create an environment that multiplies the effort of all those involved.
- It can be more efficient. The donut shop can’t have the frosting person frost whenever it’s convenient. They have to frost right after the donuts come out of the fryer. Many processes depend on the right people being in the right place at the right time.
One form of this efficiency is that the contributor can see, in real time, how the recipient responds and act accordingly.
- It offers command, control and (one kind of) inspection.
But it has costs and risks:
- Energy also spirals down. When a team member is emotionally disconnected or physically absent, the entire interaction can suffer.
- It can be less efficient. There’s less room for slack and resilience, and assembling the right people at the right time comes at a premium. There’s a lot of sitting around on a movie set.
- It doesn’t usually match the needs of the worker or the market.
- It makes it difficult to be intentional and clear about the details of the work or the arc of the project.
The implications are everywhere we look, and the status quo works to maintain its sync or async status.
Media companies that are in love with whatever sync/async built their organization often flounder when the media consumption axis flips. The only reason Amazon and Netflix exist is that their sync predecessors couldn’t figure out how to deal with an async relationship with the customer. And now that Netflix has a huge advantage, they’re timid about shifting some of the content to a sync model that would create more buzz… and Amazon has failed to capture the real-time shopping experience that’s so common online in China.
When we were forced to work from home six years ago, offices freaked out. Some embraced the async magic it offered, while many bosses were at a loss on how to manage people they couldn’t see in real time.
One reason is that employees had been indoctrinated in the idea that work was what you did when someone was watching. If you were ‘working’ from home, it was okay to also do errands and a workout, because without a hall monitor, you were off the clock.
On the other hand, some used the freedom the way a productive writer does. Without the distractions of real-time sync, there was plenty of time to get some actual work done.
Once you see it, all sorts of new insights come to mind:
The handoffs. Much of the leverage and the friction in our modern world lives at the points where work switches modes. A deadline, for example, is a sync point imposed on async work.
Who owns the clock? Sync is more than a scheduling choice, it’s also a display of power. The person who calls the meeting has already decided to spend everyone else’s time. Bosses call meetings; the employee sends a memo.
Async moves power from the coordinator to the creator.
Flips are opportunities. Why are college applications async, while job interviews are sync? Kickstarter turned product launches async, and Ted Turner turned news into something that broke.
Fake async. Over time, async creeps toward sync. It’s ironic that Slack messages, texts and email which succeeded because they were async, now create an expectation of real-time response. These are async tools used with sync expectations, so you get the interruptions of sync without its energy.
Name it. Protect your work style and the expectations for what you deliver. Organizations can be more mindful of the cost of sync, and creators can properly price their effort for each kind of work. There’s a reason it costs a million dollars to have Bob Dylan sing at your birthday party.
Sync creates cultural side effects. When everyone at the watercooler is talking about the same thing, cultural cohesion follows. When Netflix moved to binge viewing, they used their capital advantage to make it very hard for others to keep up by producing enough shows. But by sticking with this moat, they’ve diminished word of mouth. Far more people talked about Nathan Fielder’s movie during launch week than ever talked about his streaming show.
AI is currently async. An agent never needs a meeting and works at 3 a.m., so humans become the sync bottleneck. But as its power increases, expect AI to be a partner in most sync events.
Trust is built in sync and spent in async. Async works better between people who already know each other. New teams, new hires, and new customer relationships may need sync at first. The alternative is to build systems that are async by nature, enabling new participants to earn trust in powerful new ways. Online reputation systems and thoughtful online communities are getting better at this.
Here are three simple axioms to start the process with:
- Don’t make something synchronized unless it delivers valuable advantages over work done asynchronously. Show your work and defend your choice.
- When you’re doing async work, match it to your internal chemistry. Get more done, but in a different order than it’s assigned.
- Pay attention to the shifts from one to another. That’s where opportunities and pitfalls lie.
results.summary:
Understanding the fundamental differences between synchronized and asynchronized work allows individuals and organizations to optimize productivity, manage energy levels, and strategically allocate resources for better professional outcomes.

### Key Points
- Synchronized work requires participants to be present simultaneously, offering real-time collaboration and energy multiplication at the cost of flexibility and efficiency.
- Asynchronized work allows individuals to complete tasks on their own schedules, enabling better alignment with personal energy levels and deeper focus.
- The transition between sync and async modes often creates friction, as seen in the shift from traditional network television to on-demand streaming services.
- Power dynamics are often reflected in scheduling, as those who call meetings exert control over the time and attention of others.
- Modern communication tools like Slack and email often suffer from "fake async," where tools designed for flexibility are misused to demand immediate, real-time responses.
- Trust is typically established through synchronized interactions, while asynchronized workflows are most effective once professional relationships are already solidified.

### Why it Matters
Distinguishing between these two work styles helps organizations reduce the hidden costs of unnecessary meetings and prevents the burnout associated with constant, real-time availability. By intentionally choosing the right mode for specific tasks, teams can improve both their operational efficiency and the quality of their creative output.

results.title: Apple Wins Big in CNET’s People’s Picks Awards for Its MacBooks
results.author: Dashia Milden
results.content:
Of all of the laptop brands to choose from, CNET readers say Apple’s signature MacBooks really live up to the hype.
We recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to find out what they think about their laptop and the brand behind it to help you make a more sound choice on the laptop you may be considering over the holidays. We listed several well-known names, including Dell, Lenovo — and Apple. We asked about everything that matters most on a daily basis, like battery life, durability and even its performance for handling tasks like gaming and graphics. Out of 10 categories, Apple swept up eight of the awards and claimed the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Picks award.
Here’s what readers say Apple gets right when it comes to its laptops, what the experts think about Apple’s landslide win and other brands worth considering.
More from CNET
CNET’s Overall People’s Pick for Laptops Winner: Apple
Apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple users saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.
Apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.
Premium laptop
How much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple users paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” said Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.
If you plan to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — currently MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.
Cost for value
Apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple users said their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.
Digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple users seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.
Take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple users may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.
Long battery life
Battery life is a big deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook users saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.
Comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo users say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test shows that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.
Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its users either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.
“Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” said Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook users have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.
High-grade design
Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.
And MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple users reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their issues. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.
Our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.
“Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” said Goldman.
Lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it says encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.
Efficiency and productivity
When it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple users reported poor performance.
Here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without issues or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.
On the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple users rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.
The top chosen brand
Apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple users planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.
Usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.
Asus
Midrange-priced laptop
Asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.
If you’re planning to spend that amount on a new laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus users say they’re extremely satisfied.
Asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. For example, the Zenbook A14 has a thin, lightweight design that’s rigid, with long battery life and an OLED display with strong contrast and color performance. This Copilot Plus PC sells for $1,600 (but retailers like Best Buy regularly have it on sale for less). Comparatively, these premium features from other brands could cost more or sacrifice important must-have features for the price.
Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.
Acer
Budget-friendly laptop
Over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. Yet, 44% of Acer users say their laptop has exceptional value, while 50% say the value is fair — bringing a total positive cost-to-value score of over 94%. Acer also has an overall satisfaction score of 92.6% — the highest of non-Apple laptop brands.
If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. It has a big 16-inch screen but is still lightweight (3.5 pounds). And it has good battery life (over 21 hours on CNET’s battery drain test). There are a few other pluses, like the 1440p web camera that may be good for video conferencing and a sizable touchpad. All of those features and more add up to $700, which could make it a good computer for work or casual browsing. If you’re looking to spend slightly less, its predecessor, the Aspire 14 AI, is originally $639, but you may be able to score deals on both models during holiday sales.
These laptop brands are still worth considering
Even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Here are a few non-Apple laptop brands that are runner-ups to CNET’s People’s Picks winners that you shouldn’t count out of your laptop search.
Lenovo
Battery life
Lenovo is best known for packing a powerful laptop into a compact design with tablet functionality, like its Yoga line, and its durable ThinkPad business models. But CNET readers with Lenovo laptops say the brand’s battery life stands out most compared with other non-MacBook laptops.
Survey findings show that 16% of Lenovo owners say their laptops can run for 8 hours or more. And 10.5% say their laptop battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours, while 6% say their Lenovo laptops can withstand at least 10 hours before needing a charge. That’s more than what readers say about other non-Apple brands. The Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition lasts 25 hours and 45 minutes — making it one of the best laptop batteries CNET experts have tested.
Goldman said Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.
High-grade design
If your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a new laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners said they haven’t had any hardware issues with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.
Beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.
If you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. And the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 is a business laptop with Lenovo’s well-known X1 Carbon exterior and new Space Frame design, which Elliott says makes it easier to repair or replace parts if needed.
The top chosen brand
Many Lenovo laptop users are loyal to the brand, which speaks to the overall positive satisfaction rating of 83%. If Lenovo owners were in the market for a new laptop, nearly three in four (73.2%) say they would buy another Lenovo laptop. Breaking down the percentage, 33.6% say they would buy the same model again. Meanwhile, 39.6% would buy a different model but stick to Lenovo.
Here’s why that might be. Lenovo offers a plethora of options to choose from based on your needs — while still evolving its laptops. For instance, the Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 has an open M.2 slot for a second storage drive and an OLED screen for crisp, colorful images — making it perfect for gaming. Its Yoga two-in-ones let you seamlessly switch between a tablet and traditional laptop, while Lenovo’s ThinkPad and ThinkBook business laptops offer everything from ultralight 2-pound bodies to expanding rollable screens. And its new designs don’t sacrifice the must-have needs like long battery life, durability and chip efficiency that lend to strong performance.
Asus
Value for the investment
Asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It’s super thin and lightweight, but it’s still sturdy thanks to its Ceralumnium body. Plus, it has supreme 24-hour battery life, 1TB of storage and an OLED display — all for $1,200. While that’s more expensive than some laptops, it’s what’s included in that price that makes it worthwhile compared with other non-Apple laptop brands.
Efficiency and productivity
Asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. That’s followed by 40.4% of Asus laptop owners who say it has very good task performance. When it comes to tasks, 37% primarily use their Asus laptops for work, while 5% use theirs for gaming.
Asus is well known for having lightweight laptops with all-day-and-night battery life and stunning display quality. Asus laptops like the Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 have a good port selection, which could be good for gaming, work or simply connecting different devices without the need for additional adapters. And the Asus Zenbook S 14 has a strong neural processing unit that contributes to its high-speed AI performance.
Display quality
Asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. One common thread we noticed in Asus laptops is their OLED screens, which deliver high-resolution video and graphics. Asus laptops also combine stunning display quality with excellent performance and at surprisingly low prices for all of their features.
For example, the Asus Zenbook 14 isn’t the highest-quality OLED we’ve seen, but it still produces clear text and graphics on a 14-inch screen, along with exceptional black levels, Elliott said. That’s still better than LCDs that many other non-MacBooks have, and could be the reason Asus owners rate it so highly in this category.
Dell
Premium laptop
Dell wins our readers over as a top choice for high-end laptops. One-third (33.3%) of Dell owners spent over $1,500, and of that percentage, 15.2% spent over $2,000.
Dell’s premium laptops largely cater to business and gaming with their standout features and performance. The Alienware 16X Aurora is Dell’s midrange gaming laptop with user-replaceable RAM, a bright display and strong performance for $2,280. But if you want more gaming features, Dell has the Alienware 16 Area-51, which has even better gaming performance, upgradable RAM and three SSD slots for $2,530. And if you’re looking for a non-Mac alternative that comes close to MacBook quality and performance, the higher-end Dell XPS 14 is the one to choose. It has the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 graphics and 1TB of storage for $1,950.
Methodology
CNET commissioned Alchemer to conduct the People’s Picks survey to compile data. The survey was carried out online, and all figures are from Alchemer. The total sample comprised 1,003 adults. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus). Fieldwork was undertaken from Sept. 1 to Oct. 10, 2026.
results.summary:
Apple secured the top spot in CNET’s 2026 People’s Picks awards, outperforming competitors across eight categories including overall satisfaction, battery life, display quality, and hardware reliability.

### Key Points
- Apple achieved a 96.7% overall satisfaction rating, with 68% of MacBook owners stating they would purchase the same model again.
- Survey data indicates 44.4% of MacBook users experience battery life of eight hours or more, significantly outpacing Lenovo, Dell, and HP.
- Despite higher price points, 94.6% of Apple users reported that their laptops provide exceptional or fair value for the investment.
- Asus earned recognition as a top midrange choice, while Acer was highlighted for budget-friendly value and Lenovo for hardware durability.
- The survey, conducted by Alchemer, gathered insights from 1,003 U.S. adults between September and October 2026.

### Why it Matters
These findings highlight a strong consumer preference for premium hardware and ecosystem integration, which continues to drive high brand loyalty for Apple despite the availability of cheaper alternatives. For shoppers, the data suggests that while non-Apple brands like Asus and Acer offer competitive value and specific performance strengths, Apple remains the market leader in long-term user satisfaction and reliability.

results.title: Google will let schools turn off AI, but they'll have to give up Search too
results.author: sanujb6@gmail.com (Sanuj Bhatia) , Sanuj Bhatia
results.content:
What you need to know
- Google will disable Gemini and other AI tools by default for K-12 student accounts starting in 2027.
- Schools can manually enable individual AI services, but disabling AI will also remove access to Google Search.
- Schools that enable AI will get "Guided Learning" tools designed to help students solve problems instead of giving direct answers.
Google has announced a major policy change that will disable access to its AI tools, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Gemini Classroom, by default for K-12 student accounts.
Google has been pushing AI tools into pretty much every product it offers for a while now, but there have also been growing concerns about how these tools affect the learning process, especially for younger students.
And now, in a bid to give schools more control over AI use, Google announced on Tuesday that it will disable access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini Classroom, and even Google Search by default for K-12 student accounts (via The New York Times).
School administrators will still have the option to enable these services individually if they want, but they'll remain disabled by default starting in 2027.
The catch, however, is that schools won't be able to completely block Google's AI tools while keeping access to regular Google Search. Google says AI is now so deeply integrated into Search through features like AI Overviews and AI Mode that disabling AI will also mean losing access to Google Search altogether.
Chris Phillips, Google's vice president of education, told The New York Times that Search and AI are now deeply integrated. He added that schools choosing to disable Google's AI features will also lose access to Search, with students instead seeing a message explaining that the service isn't available through their school.
For schools that do decide to enable AI, Google is also introducing a new "Guided Learning" experience within Gemini and Search. Instead of simply giving students direct answers, the feature is designed to walk them through problems step by step, helping them understand how to arrive at the answer rather than just copying it.

Google says the policy change is intended to give schools more choice over which services students can access, allowing administrators to enable or disable tools based on their requirements.
But there's a pretty big contradiction here. On one hand, Google says it's giving schools more control over AI in classrooms. On the other, schools that don't want students using AI Overviews or AI Mode will also have to give up regular Google Search.
So, schools are technically getting more control over Google's AI tools, but only if they're willing to lose access to one of the most widely used search engines in the process. And that seems like a pretty strange way of giving schools more choice.
Sanuj is a tech writer who loves exploring smartphones, tablets, and wearables. He began his journey with a Nokia Lumia and later dived deep into Android and iPhone. He's been writing about tech since 2018, with bylines at Pocketnow, Android Police, Pocket-Lint, and MakeUseOf. When he's not testing gadgets, he's either sipping chai, watching football, or playing cricket.

results.title: Judge Sides With Harvard in Gino’s Tenure Case
results.author: colleen.flaherty
results.content:
Pat Greenhouse/The Boston Globe/Getty Images
A federal judge this week ruled in favor of Harvard University in a civil case brought by Francesca Gino, a former tenured professor of business there who studied ethics and was herself accused of fabricating data. Granting summary judgment to Harvard on counts including breach of contract and sex-based discrimination, U.S. District Judge Myong J. Joun wrote in his decision that “no reasonable jury could conclude on the identified evidence that Harvard revoked tenure dishonestly or without a reasonable basis, prematurely removed Gino from her appointment, or materially violated a contractual procedure.”
Further, Joun wrote—making clear he was not weighing in on Gino’s research conduct—“the record does not demonstrate any other evidence of a pattern or practice of discriminatory conduct or unfavorable treatment that can be applied to reasonably infer gender bias against Plaintiff.” Joun previously dismissed Gino’s defamation claims on the grounds that she is a public figure and did not prove malice on the part of her accusers. Joun noted this week that his decision does not affect Harvard’s separate defamation counterclaim.
Early research misconduct allegations against Gino were raised by the blog Data Colada. Harvard placed her on leave in 2023 and revoked her tenure in 2025. Gino, who has denied engaging in research misconduct, filed a $25 million lawsuit against Data Colada, Harvard and her former dean. Related claims against the Data Colada team were previously dismissed. This week’s decision dismissed all remaining claims against the dean as well. Gino’s current attorneys did not respond immediately to a request for comment Tuesday. Disgruntled Harvard alum Bill billionaire Ackman publicly backed Gino’s battle.
results.summary:
A federal judge granted summary judgment to Harvard University, dismissing a $25 million lawsuit filed by former professor Francesca Gino regarding her tenure revocation and discrimination allegations.

### Key Points
- U.S. District Judge Myong J. Joun ruled that Harvard acted within its contractual rights when revoking Gino’s tenure in 2025.
- The court found no evidence of gender-based discrimination or procedural violations in the university's handling of the case.
- Gino, a former business professor, faced research misconduct allegations initially raised by the blog Data Colada in 2023.
- All remaining claims against the former dean were dismissed, though Harvard’s separate defamation counterclaim against Gino remains active.
- Previous defamation claims brought by Gino against the university and the Data Colada team were dismissed in earlier proceedings.

### Why it Matters
This ruling reinforces the legal protections universities maintain when enforcing academic integrity standards and internal disciplinary procedures. The outcome sets a significant precedent for how institutions manage high-profile research misconduct cases and potential litigation from tenured faculty.

results.title: "An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process," Nexus Mods say as they rule out barring generated creations from their site
results.author: Mark Warren
results.content:
The owners of Nexus Mods have ruled out instituting an outright ban on AI-generated works being uploaded the site, instead opting to expand their current rules on modders disclosing how they've used AI in making their mods. This latest move to address the waves of AI-created or AI-thumbnailed mods now hitting Nexus Mods on a daily basis follows Nexus' modus operandi up to this point, which has been simply to try and ensure AI usage is clearly labelled so prospective downloaders can make informed decisions.
"We won't introduce an outright ban on AI-generated mods," Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann wrote in a news post. "You may ask me why, since that is not the solution some of you were looking for. The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable. An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process, but will prevent people from mentioning its use. We'd prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform.
"This doesn't mean that any work done using AI will get removed; AI-generated mods are welcome on our platform provided that they meet certain criteria regarding permissions, transparency, presentation, and conduct. Mod Authors should have a chance to decide about the further use of their work, and you should be able to decide for yourselves how much AI-based content you want to see, whether more, less, or no content at all.
"As for our own position: Nexus Mods will not use your mods to train AI and will not sell or license them to anyone doing so. We refused to do that in the past, and we will refuse to do so in the future. Given such a variety of opinions within our community, not everyone will agree with any decision taken. These are the ones we believe are right for Nexus Mods today, and we’ll keep adjusting them as the tools evolve and as we see how these changes work in practice, with your feedback guiding that."
In terms of the changes which are being brought in to toughen up the site's current three tag system design to make mods containing AI-generated content, AI media, or made with AI assistance easier to spot, Nexus are making AI disclosures mandatory for those uploading new mods. "What this means is that for mods tagged as AI-assisted, we’re also introducing a requirement for a public explanation of how and where AI was used, which should give you a better understanding of what you’re downloading, rather than leaving you to make assumptions on a tag alone," Folmann wrote. "We’re also going to make AI tags on mod pages more prominent, displaying them immediately after adult-content tags so they’re easier to spot."
"While we hope these changes will encourage everyone to disclose their AI usage, to be honest, that’s not going to happen," he continued. "Additionally, we are putting clear moderation standards in place, enforced with consequences for breaking the rules." New "permission options covering AI usage and training, as well as forks and derivative mods" are also being worked on, with the hopes of giving modders more control over how their works can be reused. Finally, Folmann noted that the site are "investing in security tooling and specialised staff" to address concerns over generative AI making "bespoke malicious code hidden inside mods" more prevalent.
Mod makers are being given a 60 day grace period to make sure their existing works meet the new rules, which'll run until January 2nd.
As you can imagine, the comments section of this Nexus Mods announcement is lively. Over on LinkedIn, Folmann patted himself on the back a bit about the mixed reception being an indicator the site are going about this the right way. "Some wanted a full ban. Some think we went too far. That tells me we drew the line where the real argument is," he declared, adding that "transparency beats prohibition". He also reiterated that his vision is of "modding that's Spotify-easy to play and GitHub-powerful to create, with humans in charge".
I reckon that with or without these changes, in the absence of its owners taking a strong stand browsing Nexus Mods is going to carry on be more of an exercise in ducking dodgy stuff than it was prior to most games' pages being splattered with the likes of icky AI-baked Geralt clones standing where decent screenshots of the actual game would've been more than adequate.
results.summary:
Nexus Mods has officially rejected an outright ban on AI-generated content, choosing instead to implement mandatory disclosure requirements and stricter moderation standards for all uploaded modding projects.

### Key Points
- Nexus Mods CEO Victor Folmann confirmed that AI-generated mods remain permitted provided they meet new transparency, permission, and presentation criteria.
- Uploaders must now provide a public explanation detailing how and where AI tools were utilized in their modding process.
- AI-related tags will be displayed more prominently on mod pages, appearing immediately after adult-content warnings for better visibility.
- The platform is investing in specialized security staff and tools to detect potential malicious code generated by AI.
- Mod authors have a 60-day grace period ending January 2, 2025, to update existing uploads to comply with the new disclosure rules.
- Nexus Mods explicitly stated it will not use user-submitted content to train AI models or license such data to third-party developers.

### Why it Matters
This policy shift highlights the ongoing challenge of balancing creative freedom with user transparency in the rapidly evolving landscape of generative AI. By prioritizing disclosure over prohibition, Nexus Mods aims to maintain platform control while allowing the community to make informed decisions about the content they download.

results.title: ‘I’m 100 Percent at War with Trump’: MAGA Revolts After Midterms Wipeout
results.author: David Gilbert
results.content:
Many MAGAworld figures are already pointing the finger of blame for their midterm losses squarely at President Donald Trump and his policies.
Trump spent Tuesday evening lashing out at Fox News for platforming the Democrats who swept aside their GOP opponents in deep red states and took control of the House and Senate.
“[Fox] bears responsibility for these losses by constantly and consistently putting on the Dumocrat opposition, and worse,” the president wrote on Truth Social. Later in the night, he called in to Fox News, where he congratulated the Democrats on their results.
Trump made clear that he doesn’t think the historic blowout was a reflection of his popularity, writing, “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” He then posted a picture of a red baseball hat with the word VETO embossed on the front.
But in the hours that followed, MAGA revolted.
Matt Walsh, a right-wing podcaster, called the results “a political catastrophe of historic proportions” and Trump “an 80-year-old lame-duck president.” Walsh blamed Trump’s decision to start a war with Iran and his focus on trivial matters like attempting to rename artificial intelligence super intelligence and the White House ballroom.
For right-wing commentator Mike Cernovich, it was Trump’s decision to ostracize libertarian voters that was partly to blame.
Mike Flynn, the disgraced former national security adviser who was among the most prominent voices pushing bogus conspiracies about the 2020 election being stolen, also blamed Trump, writing on X, “Someone needs to look in a mirror.” Flynn also blamed Christians for not showing up to vote.
But noted conspiracy theorist Alex Jones had another take on why Trump was to blame.
“I think he’s a Democrat. I’m gonna just say it right now,” Jones said on his show Tuesday night. “I’ve tried to salvage Trump. I’ve not been sure. I’ve invested so much—maybe I was blind to it—I think he’s the ultimate Democrat sleeper cell, and he works for them. I’m 100 percent at war with Trump.”
Other MAGA figures like right-wing commentators Jack Posobiec and Nick Sortor both blamed Trump’s decision to start a war with Iran for the losses but didn’t directly name Trump in their posts.
Unsurprisingly, Marjorie Taylor Greene, the former congresswoman who broke decisively with Trump earlier this year, also blamed the president. “Tonight was a total referendum on Trump. He told people to vote like he was on the ballot and they did,” Greene wrote on X.
One notable aspect of MAGAworld’s response to Tuesday’s GOP wipeout was the relative silence coming from some of Trump’s biggest supporters.
Elon Musk, who poured hundreds of millions of dollars into supporting losing Republican candidates, has not said who was to blame for the results. He did post a joke saying his “election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time” and commented that it was “interesting” that an exit poll showed the Iran war was a “massive losing issue.”
Rogan O’Handley, a vocal MAGA influencer known as DC Draino who posts incessantly on X about politics, has also not reacted publicly to the results. Speaker of the House Mike Johnson, who was reelected on Tuesday night, said the results were “not what we’d hoped and fought for” but failed to say what or who was to blame.
White House deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser Stephen Miller has also not commented publicly on the results, but his wife, Katie Miller, who boosted election conspiracy theories earlier on Tuesday, laid the blame on the media, which she called “a propaganda arm of the woke left.”
There were, however, a few right-wing figures who continued to publicly support Trump despite the losses, including MAGA influencer Laura Loomer, who wrote, “President Trump is a hero for stopping Iran from having a nuclear weapon, and now he should finish the job.” Instead of blaming Trump, Loomer spent Tuesday evening lamenting the end of America and the rise of communism.
Another right-wing figure continuing to back Trump was the former Fox News host turned conspiracy theorist Lara Logan, who blamed an anonymous group of Republicans who conspired to bring about the defeat so they could “get rid of the MAGA movement and the establishment would retake the party.”
Chaya Raichik, who runs the hugely popular LibsofTikTok accounts, blamed the losses on a years-long Democrat plot to import “millions of foreigners.”
Kari Lake, Trump’s nominee for ambassador to Jamaica, also refused to lay the blame at the president’s feet and was one of the few election deniers who continued to boost claims of a stolen election. “America, do you think that our elections are honest? Do you have complete confidence that only legal votes were counted?” Lake wrote in the early hours of Wednesday morning.
Others, like Harrison Smith, a host on Steve Bannon’s War Room show, turned their ire on their fellow right-wing influencers. He blamed Loomer, Ben Shapiro, Mark Levin, Will Chamberlain, and AIPAC, the prominent lobbying organization, for the losses.
But at least one former Trumpworld figure did take the blame on themselves. Former homeland security secretary Kristi Noem posted on X that the massive losses happened because “we were too successful in the first year of the Trump administration.”
results.summary:
Prominent MAGA figures and right-wing commentators are publicly blaming Donald Trump for significant Republican losses in the recent midterm elections, sparking a major internal movement revolt.

### Key Points
- Donald Trump blamed Fox News for the GOP losses, while influencers like Matt Walsh and Mike Cernovich criticized Trump’s policy focus and alienation of libertarian voters.
- Alex Jones labeled Trump a "Democrat sleeper cell," and former adviser Mike Flynn suggested the former president should "look in a mirror" regarding the results.
- Marjorie Taylor Greene described the election outcome as a "total referendum on Trump," noting that his influence directly impacted voter turnout and party performance.
- Elon Musk and Speaker Mike Johnson remained notably silent on assigning blame, while others like Kari Lake continued to promote claims of election interference.
- Some supporters, including Laura Loomer and Lara Logan, defended Trump, attributing the defeat to external factors like the media, immigration, or internal party conspiracies.

### Why it Matters
The public fracturing of the MAGA movement signals a potential shift in the Republican Party's internal power dynamics following a major electoral defeat. This internal conflict could influence future candidate selection and the party's strategic direction as prominent figures debate the viability of Trump's continued leadership.

results.title: Certified Android TV manufacturer put unauthorized backdoor in 1.3 million set-top boxes, Google reveals — OEM sold access to criminal affiliates, used massive network as botnet for ad fraud, residential proxy
results.author: editors@tomshardware.com (Jowi Morales) , Jowi Morales
results.content:
Google just shut down a massive botnet operation involving an OEM and ODM manufacturer. According to the company blog, Videostrong Technology Co., which was a certified Android TV partner, purposefully installed a backdoor into 1.3 million set-top boxes and then sold access to criminal affiliates. This allowed for the installation of hidden software that the bad actors could use to conduct ad fraud, build residential proxy networks, and even remotely install malware on the device itself to target the end-user.
“Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices,” the company said in the Google Cloud blog post. It also added, “We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates. We believe this campaign wasn’t an isolated rogue insider or a development oversight. As a result, Google has cut ties with Videostrong and banned them from making devices with preloaded Google apps.”
While Google did not mention when Videostrong started loading malware into its products, the company said that the pre-installed malware evolved into a complex, three-stage design in 2024. This meant that the manufacturer has been exploiting millions of devices for years now, with the latest developments designed to make the malware more resilient and allow for multiple bad actors to take advantage of the system. Even though the company has already terminated its business relationship with Videostrong, the open-source nature of Android means that it could continue using the operating system on its products.
There have been supply chain attacks in the past, wherein a third-party compromises a trusted product to steal data, like some Ledger hardware wallets that have been sold by a reseller in Southeast Asia and Europe. Although Google did not characterize this as a supply chain attack, as it was perpetrated by the manufacturer itself and not a third-party operator, it still compromised a supposedly trusted operating system, leading to millions of victims. This incident also shows how even the simplest of devices can be used to execute complicated attacks, like how a Chinese couple hid a PC behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel and targeted 2.4 million victims.

Google has terminated its partnership with manufacturer Videostrong Technology after discovering the company embedded backdoors into 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes to facilitate global cybercriminal activities.

### Key Points
- Videostrong Technology pre-installed malicious backdoors into 1.3 million Android TV devices to enable ad fraud and residential proxy networks.
- The manufacturer sold access to these infected devices to criminal affiliates, allowing for the remote installation of additional malware.
- Google confirmed the malicious software evolved into a complex, three-stage design throughout 2024 to evade detection.
- Google has officially banned Videostrong from producing devices that include preloaded Google applications or services.
- The compromised hardware was sold under various brands and models over several years, impacting a significant global user base.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights a critical vulnerability in the consumer electronics supply chain where manufacturers can compromise device security at the firmware level. It raises significant concerns regarding the integrity of pre-installed software and the long-term security risks posed by untrusted hardware partners in the Android ecosystem.
